Yes: several papers address stopping student models from becoming too wordy or repetitive during on-policy distillation. One focuses on length inflation and repetition saturation in OPD, proposing a reference-based divergence constraint plus rollout mixture distillation to prevent truncation collapse [1]. Another finds termination-token mismatch as a source of excessive length and mitigates it by treating functionally equivalent EOS tokens as a shared stopping action [2]. A third directly notes that stronger revision can make responses too verbose and uses shorter verified rewrites to reduce output length [3].

If you want methods specifically about controlling generation during distillation, early stopping rollout restricts rollout generation to the first response tokens and improves stability [4], while student-in-the-loop selection prunes unhelpful branches during generation [8].
